steps.name: Stage 1 — Merge Raw Tables
steps.description: Joins collision.csv + vehicle.csv + casualty.csv at casualty level. Drops 9 leakage columns and ~35 irrelevant columns. Splits 80/20 grouped by collision_index (GroupShuffleSplit). Converts all features to numeric.
steps.why: Creates the clean, analysis-ready dataset from 3 raw sources. Group-aware split prevents same-crash casualties leaking across train/test.

steps.name: Stage 2 — Train Linear Regression
steps.description: Trains Linear Regression to predict number_of_casualties from 5 collision-level features (speed_limit, road_type, junction_detail, light_conditions, weather_conditions). Uses 5-fold OOF predictions to avoid leakage. Saves model, OOF predictions, and metrics.
steps.why: One of two candidate models for generating the risk_score feature. OOF ensures the risk_score on training rows was never seen during training.

steps.name: Stage 2 — Train Decision Tree Regressor
steps.description: Trains Decision Tree Regressor on the same 5 collision-level features. Same 5-fold OOF approach as Linear Regression.
steps.why: Second candidate model. Compared against LR by R-squared to pick the winner.

steps.name: Stage 2 — Compare Regressors & Generate risk_score
steps.description: Compares LR vs DT by R-squared, picks the winner (LR, R2=0.023). Maps OOF risk_score onto train rows (no leakage). Retrains winner on full train set and predicts risk_score for test rows. Overwrites merged CSVs with the new risk_score column (18 -> 19 cols).
steps.why: The risk_score feature is the bridge between Stage 2 regression and Stage 3A classification. It gives the classifiers a continuous signal about expected casualty count.

steps.name: Stage 3A Phase A — Out-of-Fold Meta-Feature Generation
steps.description: 5-fold StratifiedGroupKFold CV with 3 base classifiers (Logistic Regression, KNN k=15, Decision Tree). Each training row gets probability predictions from a model that never saw it. All 15 temporary models (3 x 5 folds) are destroyed. Output: 9 probability columns + risk_score + target.
steps.why: Creates leak-free training data for the meta-classifier. If we predicted on training data directly, the meta-classifier would learn to trust overconfident base model predictions and fail on test data.

steps.name: Stage 3A Phase B — Train Final Base Models & Generate meta_test

steps.why: These final models produce the test-side meta-features and are the actual models loaded at inference time in the Streamlit app.

steps.name: Stage 4 — Train Meta-Classifier
steps.description: Trains stacking meta-classifier (Logistic Regression, class_weight=balanced) on exactly 10 features: 9 base model probabilities + risk_score. Evaluates on held-out test set. Saves confusion matrix.
steps.why: This is the final prediction model. It learns the optimal weighting of 3 classifiers' opinions plus the regression risk score.

steps.why: This is the payoff — the answer to 'does the multi-stage pipeline beat a single model?' Also checks Fatal-class recall, the most safety-critical metric.
